title: BECE English Studies: Grammar & Structure - English Studies - Direct and Indirect Speech
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Change the following sentence to indirect speech:
"I am going to the market," she said.
options: She said that she is going to the market.
She said that I am going to the market.
She said that she was going to the market.
She says that she was going to the market.
questions.explain: When reporting speech in the past ('said'), the present continuous tense ('am going') shifts back one tense to past continuous ('was going'). The pronoun 'I' also changes to 'she'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
What is the correct reported speech for the following command?
"Sit down!" the teacher commanded the student.
options: The teacher commanded the student to sit down.
The teacher said the student to sit down.
The teacher commanded the student sitting down.
The teacher told the student that he should sit down.
questions.explain: To report a direct command, we use a reporting verb (commanded/ordered/told) + object + to-infinitive. Thus, 'commanded the student to sit down' is the standard rule.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correct direct speech for the sentence:
He asked me where I lived.
options: "Where do you live?" he asked me.
"Where did you lived?" he asked me.
"Where you live?" he asked me.
"Where are you living?" he asked me.
questions.explain: In indirect speech, the simple past ('lived') originates from the simple present in direct speech. Therefore, the direct question should use the simple present: 'Where do you live?'
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Change the following direct question into indirect speech:
He asked her, "Did you finish the assignment?"
options: He asked her if she had finished the assignment.
He asked her if she finished the assignment.
He asked her whether she has finished the assignment.
He asked her that did she finish the assignment.
questions.explain: For yes/no questions, use 'if' or 'whether'. The simple past tense ('Did you finish') in direct speech changes to the past perfect tense ('had finished') in indirect speech.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Convert this exclamation to indirect speech:
The old man said, "Alas! I have lost my only key."
options: The old man said alas that he had lost his only key.
The old man exclaimed with joy that he had lost his only key.
The old man exclaimed with sorrow that he had lost his only key.
The old man exclaimed that he has lost his only key.
questions.explain: Exclamatory sentences with words like 'Alas!' are reported using 'exclaimed with sorrow/grief'. The present perfect ('have lost') shifts to past perfect ('had lost').
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
What is the correct reported speech for the following sentence?
The teacher said, "The earth revolves around the sun."
options: The teacher said that the earth revolves around the sun.
The teacher said that the earth revolved around the sun.
The teacher says that the earth revolved around the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had revolved around the sun.
questions.explain: If the direct speech states a universal truth, a scientific fact, or a habitual action, the tense inside the reported clause does not change, even if the reporting verb ('said') is in the past.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correctly reported sentence:
John said, "I will call you tomorrow."
options: John said that he would call me tomorrow.
John said that he will call me the next day.
John said that he would call me the next day.
John said that he could call me the next day.
questions.explain: In indirect speech, the modal 'will' changes to 'would', and the time expression 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day' or 'the following day'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Convert this statement into indirect speech:
Mary said, "I will go to the library now."
options: Mary said that she will go to the library now.
Mary said that she would go to the library then.
Mary says that she would go to the library then.
Mary said that I would go to the library now.
questions.explain: In reported speech, 'will' changes to 'would', 'I' changes to 'she' to match the speaker, and the time indicator 'now' changes to 'then'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correct indirect speech for the following question:
The teacher asked me, "Why are you late?"
options: The teacher asked me why I was late.
The teacher asked me why was I late.
The teacher asked me why am I late.
The teacher asked me why I am late.
questions.explain: In indirect questions, the sentence structure changes from a question format (verb before subject) to a statement format (subject before verb). Also, the present tense 'are' shifts back to the past tense 'was'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
How is the following negative command reported in indirect speech?
The guard shouted, "Do not touch the electrical wires!"
options: The guard shouted that we do not touch the electrical wires.
The guard shouted to not touch the electrical wires.
The guard shouted not to touch the electrical wires.
The guard shouted us to don't touch the electrical wires.
questions.explain: To report a negative command, use the structure: reporting verb + object + 'not to' + infinitive.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which of the following is the correct direct speech for this sentence?
He said that he had seen the movie the day before.
options: He said, "I have seen the movie yesterday."
He said, "I saw the movie yesterday."
He said, "I saw the movie the day before."
He said, "I had seen the movie yesterday."
questions.explain: In indirect speech, 'the day before' represents 'yesterday' from direct speech. The past perfect 'had seen' originates from the simple past 'saw' when combined with a specific past time marker like 'yesterday'.
questions.subject: English Studies
